gloss: Learn one thing and infer three others.
teaser: Ever wonder how a single lesson can lead to broader understanding?
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever wonder how a single lesson can lead to broader understanding? [break 1s] The phrase is: 举一反三, jǔ yī fǎn sān. [break 1s] 举 (jǔ) means 'to raise' or 'to lift' [break 0.5s] 一 (yī) means 'one' [break 0.5s] 反 (fǎn) means 'to reflect' or 'to reverse' [break 0.5s] 三 (sān) means 'three' [break 0.5s] Together, it suggests 'learn one thing and infer three others.' [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originates from Chinese educational philosophy, where students are encouraged to draw broader conclusions from individual teachings. It emphasizes critical thinking and applying knowledge to different contexts, promoting a deeper understanding of concepts. The idea is that if you understand one principle well, you can figure out several related ideas. [break 1.5s] Example 1: 学完这道题后，我能举一反三。 [break 1s] After learning this problem, I can infer three others. [break 1s] Example 2: 他用这个方法举一反三，解决了其他问题。 [break 1s] He used this method to infer three others and solved the other problems. [break 1s] Example 3: 老师鼓励我们举一反三，掌握更多知识。 [break 1s] The teacher encourages us to learn one thing and infer three others to master more knowledge. [break 1s] So, remember, 举一反三 means to learn one thing and infer three others. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
